evidence.field: 形義通解: 國 graphic structure
evidence.text: The entry analyzes bronze 國 as 囗 plus phonetic 或; 囗 represents a country’s boundary or territory, and the stated original sense is ‘country/state’. Warring States forms may use 匚 or 𠃊 in place of 囗 while retaining a region/boundary marker role.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 形義通解: early use and semantic attestations
evidence.text: CUHK reports 國 with 囗 in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, used for the country sense, and gives bronze examples from the 彔卣 and 蔡侯鐘. It separately reports 或 used for 國 in bronze inscriptions, citing He zun’s 宅茲中或; one interpretation reads 或 as 國 (‘the middle of the country’), while another takes it as 域 (‘central territory’). The inscription interpretation is disputed in the source. Later examples include Warring States bamboo slips and Han silk manuscripts using 國 for country/state, including Mawangdui texts; these attestations document usage but do not establish a sequence of sense extensions.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi entry as transcribed by CUHK
evidence.text: The transmitted Han-dynasty dictionary account says 國 means 邦 and analyzes it as 从囗从或. This is a historical account and is consistent with, but not independent proof of, the phonetic analysis reported by CUHK.
evidence.title: 國 — 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: Glyph origin: 國 phonetic series and component analysis
evidence.text: The entry classifies 國 as a phono-semantic compound, semantic 囗 plus phonetic 或. In the Zhengzhang Shangfang 2003 Old Chinese system it lists 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ, alongside multiple members of the same phonetic series; these are reconstructions, not directly attested pronunciations. This supports a phonetic relationship without requiring a claim about the original depicted object, which this research did not establish.
evidence.title: 國 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: For 國, the entry gives modern Standard Mandarin guó (Pinyin) and Guangzhou–Hong Kong Cantonese gwok3 (Jyutping). For 或, it gives modern Beijing huò (Pinyin), Middle Chinese hwok, and Old Chinese *[ɢ]ʷˁək in Baxter–Sagart 2014 system 1.1; it also lists Zhengzhang 2003 *ɡʷɯːɡ. The dossier’s 國 metadata separately lists Baxter–Sagart *[C.q]ʷˤək and Zhengzhang *kʷɯːɡ. The within-system Old Chinese reconstructions show similarity with an initial contrast; modern readings are not proof by themselves of the historical sound-component role.
evidence.title: 或 — Wiktionary

evidence.text: The entry identifies 国 as simplified from 國, with 或 replaced by 玉; it also notes unorthodox variant 囯 with 王. It identifies 国 as Japanese shinjitai paired with kyūjitai 國. This is a graphic-form account and does not make 玉 the historical phonetic element of 國.
evidence.title: 国 — Wiktionary

evidence.source: State Council resolution reproduced at Wikisource
evidence.text: The reproduced resolution is dated 28 January 1956 and says first-table simplified characters were to be used from 1 February 1956. The opened page’s first table does not include 国, so this page alone does not date the adoption of 国; it confirms the broader policy context only.
evidence.title: 国务院关于公布汉字简化方案的决议

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction supplementary materials
evidence.text: The project describes its materials as Old Chinese reconstructions and identifies the system as Baxter–Sagart 2014. This supports labeling the dossier’s *[C.q]ʷˤək as a reconstruction in that system, but the accessible PDF download could not be inspected here for the specific 國 and 或 entries.
evidence.title: The Baxter-Sagart reconstruction of Old Chinese

search_audit.query: site:humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf 國 甲骨 西周 或 國 字形; 國 earliest attestation Western Zhou bronze inscription paleography meaning 或; 國 guó Old Chinese reconstruction 或 phonetic 國 Baxter Sagart Zhengzhang
search_audit.outcome: Search performed. Opened the CUHK entry and the Baxter–Sagart project page; CUHK gave detailed structure, uses, examples, and the disputed He zun reading. The project page describes the reconstruction system; its PDF data file was not accessible as text.

search_audit.query: 國 simplified character introduced 1956 simplification list 国 玉 或 historical variant source
search_audit.outcome: Opened the State Council resolution transcript and the 国 entry. The resolution establishes the general 1956 simplification framework and date, but the visible first table does not list 国. Wiktionary reports 国 simplified from 國 by 或→玉 and identifies it as Japanese shinjitai; the exact official adoption date and the historical derivation of this replacement were not independently established.

search_audit.query: 或 國 Baxter Sagart Old Chinese pronunciation Zhengzhang phonetic component 國
search_audit.outcome: Opened both entries. They report modern readings and historical reconstructions in named systems; Zhengzhang 2003 lists 國 *kʷɯːɡ and 或 *ɡʷɯːɡ, while the dossier supplies Baxter–Sagart 國 *[C.q]ʷˤək and the 或 page lists *[ɢ]ʷˁək. The evidence supports treating 或 as phonetic in 國, with reconstructed sound correspondence rather than exact identity.

gaps: The consulted sources do not establish a recoverable name or original referent for 或’s depicted form; no claim that a weapon/tool name caused the sound borrowing is made.
CUHK reports the He zun 或 reading as 國 but also records the alternative 域 interpretation; the passage is not treated as an uncontested early attestation of 国/國.
CUHK’s page displayed images of historical script forms, but no glyph image was visually inspected in this research; graphic descriptions are source assertions.

The earliest attestation of the lexical item meaning ‘country/state’ is not settled here: the source reports Western Zhou 國 forms and bronze use of 或, but the He zun reading is disputed and no full corpus survey was conducted.
The semantic path from boundary/territory to polity, and subsequent senses such as kingdom, dynasty, or national modifier, is not established as a dated chronology by the sources opened.

The exact historical pathway from 國 to 国 (including whether 玉 replacement arose first in Chinese shorthand, Japanese usage, or another variant tradition) is not established. Wiktionary’s formal correspondence is reported without inferring ancestry beyond 國 as the source form.

The direct Baxter–Sagart downloadable reconstruction table could not be inspected, so 國’s Baxter–Sagart form is taken from dossier metadata and is not independently verified against the project dataset.
No independent modern pronunciation source was opened for Japanese or Korean readings; these dossier readings are not used to establish the graphic origin or phonetic analysis.
